opportunities.title: Front door rebuild: one agent-readable, mobile-ready path from search result to booked consultation
opportunities.problem: Every customer-facing entry point is broken or missing. The site has no viewport meta tag and a fixed ~781px table layout, so a 390px phone renders the desktop page at ~980 CSS px with tiny text; the 'FREE consultation' phone number is baked into a header image and there is no tel: link, no form, no input field and no booking anywhere on the site, so the only ways in are a landline and a personal aol.com mailbox. The Google Business Profile is unclaimed with 4 reviews at 3.0 and no photos, and the site footer and contact page say 'Located in Manalapan, NJ' while the directions page and Google give 77 Milltown Rd, East Brunswick - two addresses for one practice. Titles and metadata ('David Miller', no meta description, no JSON-LD) give neither search engines nor AI assistants anything to quote, and no hours are published anywhere on the site even though Google shows Mon-Fri 9-5.

opportunities.agent_design: Mostly a build-and-fix engagement with a thin agent layer. Scope: (1) claim and complete the Google Business Profile - correct East Brunswick address, real categories (Real estate attorney, Estate planning attorney, Tax preparation), services, hours, exterior/interior photos; (2) rebuild the five static pages as a responsive site with a viewport meta, a tel: link on every header, a short intake form (matter type: purchase / sale / refinance / 1031 / will / probate / LLC / business sale / tax return; property address or county; target closing date; best callback window) and LocalBusiness/Attorney JSON-LD carrying one canonical NAP; (3) an event-driven intake agent behind the form that classifies the inquiry into a practice area, detects conflicts-of-interest signals (other party names) for the attorney to clear, writes the enquiry into a single queue with the source attached, and sends the prospect an immediate acknowledgement with what to bring; (4) review-request agent: after a closing is marked complete, sends one review link and routes anything negative to the attorney before it is posted publicly. Human approval: the attorney approves the site's practice-area and fee wording and clears every conflict check; the agent never gives legal advice or quotes a fee.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This is four systems that do not talk to each other: a static site with no CMS, an unclaimed Google profile, no CRM or queue at all, and an aol.com inbox. A website builder produces a prettier page but not a claimable, schema-correct listing plus an intake agent that dedupes, conflict-screens and writes to a queue; a chatbot subscription cannot fix NAP, structured data or mobile layout. The conflict-screen and routing step also has to respect N.J. RPC 1.6/5.3 and leave an audit trail of who reviewed what.

impact_estimate.range: No defensible revenue range is asserted. Observable impact today: 0 of 3 agent-readiness checks pass for booking, 1 of 3 for findability; the practice is invisible to tap-to-dial, form and AI-assistant paths entirely. Secondary anchor: at most ~1-2 hours/week of staff phone handling is displaced (~$1,600-$3,200/yr at the NJ legal-secretary median of $63,080), which is the smallest part of the value.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes the owner keeps his current ~15-20 inbound enquiries a month and that a share of phone/email enquiries simply never happens because a phone user cannot tap a number in a JPEG and cannot leave a form. No NJ-specific lead-value or law-firm conversion benchmark was found, and closing fees are not public, so no revenue uplift is claimed. Dollar figure uses NJ legal-secretary median $63,080/yr, divided by 2,080 hours = ~$30.33/hr (BLS OEWS May 2025 via O*NET).

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2-3 weeks: claimed and fully populated Google profile with photos and correct hours; a 5-7 page responsive site with viewport meta, tel: links, JSON-LD and one canonical East Brunswick NAP; a live intake form plus a single shared enquiry queue with acknowledgement email; before/after copies of the mobile rendering and a one-page report of what an AI assistant can now read and quote.

opportunities.title: 24/7 intake, matter-triage and closing-aware scheduling agent
opportunities.problem: Intake and scheduling are entirely manual and phone-first for a sole practitioner who is often in closings. The home page tells prospects to 'call my office and ask to speak with me'; there is no after-hours coverage, no answering service, no chat and no portal, only a personal aol.com mailbox for async contact, and no hours are published anywhere on the site. Calendar handling is manual and visibly fragile: a 1-star Google review describes two cancelled appointments quoting the office that closings take priority, and closings are unpredictable by nature. On top of real-estate volume the owner personally prepares income tax returns in tax season, so capacity swings seasonally while the phone keeps ringing.

Legal secretaries report the scheduling/phone-repeating tasks as core duties, and 54% rate 'importance of repeating same tasks' as extremely important - https://www.onetonline.org/link/summary/43-6012.00
opportunities.agent_design: An event-driven intake agent on two triggers: inbound phone (missed-call/SMS text-back plus optional voice agent, or voicemail-to-queue) and inbound web/email enquiry. It asks a short structured set of questions (matter type, property county, contract or attorney-review deadline, other parties for conflict screening, best callback window), classifies the matter into a practice area, and routes purchase/sale/refinance leads to a booking calendar while flagging wills, probate, LLC and business-sale enquiries for attorney review. Scheduling reads the attorney's calendar (Microsoft 365/Google) and enforces rules the owner sets: closing-day blackout blocks, a buffer before any contract-review deadline, a cap on daily consultations, and tax-season capacity reduction. It drafts the confirmation, the 'what to bring' checklist and the engagement-letter packet for one-click attorney approval, and it escalates every exception - known client, deadline inside 7 days, opposing party already in the system, fee question, anything ambiguous - to a human instead of answering. All client data stays in a zero-retention/tenant-isolated deployment per N.J. RPC 1.6, and the agent never states a fee or a legal opinion.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: Booking widgets cannot classify a real-estate matter, run a conflict screen against existing clients, or know that a closing day cannot take consultations; a chatbot subscription cannot read and write the attorney's calendar or fire on a missed call. The hard parts are integration (phone/SMS, calendar, email, queue), a rules engine for deadline and closing-priority logic, and confidentiality-compliant data handling. Reliability matters more than cleverness: a wrongly booked or silently dropped consultation is worse than a voicemail.

impact_estimate.range: Roughly $5,000-$20,000/yr of attorney and staff time redirected from routine intake, scheduling and reminder calls, plus reduced reschedule churn. Time basis: 3-8 hours/week of combined secretary and attorney phone/calendar handling at $30.33-$77.61/hr (NJ medians for legal secretaries, $63,080, and lawyers, $161,430, divided by 2,080 hours).
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes 15-30 inbound enquiries a month (inference - no volume data is public), that roughly half arrive when nobody can answer live, and that 40-60% of the intake/scheduling/reminder work is routine enough to automate - the low end of the 14% average productivity lift measured on AI-assisted service agents is well below that share, so the range is deliberately conservative on volume rather than generous on the lift. No revenue uplift from recovered enquiries is claimed because closing fees are not public. Wage figures are BLS OEWS May 2025 republished by O*NET, NJ statewide, all employer types.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3-4 weeks: missed-call text-back and a web/email intake agent covering the four highest-volume matter types; a booking calendar with closing-day blackout and deadline-buffer rules; a human-approval queue for exceptions and for the engagement-letter packet; a routing-accuracy log (the conference paper on civil legal intake reached 97.37% hits@2 on 419 real queries, so measure this firm's own accuracy before going live); weekly throughput and response-time report.

opportunities.title: Closing-status and process knowledge agent that answers 'where am I?' from the firm's own files
opportunities.problem: Client communication during a transaction is ad hoc and is the exact thing clients complain about. There is no client portal, status page or document system on the site, the owner says he personally spends a lot of time explaining the whole transaction at the first meeting, and one reviewer disputes whether legal papers were ever mailed to her while another describes being rescheduled without apology. Positive reviews praise 'explanations of next steps', which means the firm's differentiator is a manual, attorney-hours activity repeated per client. The practice is document-heavy by nature - deeds, contracts, title, lender packages, 1031 exchanges, probate filings, plus seasonal tax returns - with one attorney and a couple of support staff.

General-purpose and legal-vendor LLMs still hallucinate authority materially (ChatGPT-4 ~58% on verifiable federal-case questions in a peer-reviewed study; commercial legal RAG tools 17-33% in a Stanford academic working paper), so answers must be retrieval-grounded from the firm's own documents with attorney sign-off - https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.01301 ; https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.20362 (working paper)
opportunities.agent_design: A retrieval-grounded knowledge and status agent with a per-matter checklist as its backbone. Each matter gets a milestone list (contract received, title ordered, survey, mortgage commitment, closing scheduled, deed prepared, closing held, deed recorded, funds disbursed, file closed). A staff member advances a milestone - by email flag, shared checklist or a one-line message - and the agent fires the appropriate client message: what just happened, what happens next, what the client must send, with a document request link that logs receipt. Clients can ask plain questions ('when is my closing', 'what do I need to bring', 'did you get my signed contract') and the agent answers only from that matter's file plus a firm-authored FAQ and closing-process guide; anything about legal advice, fees, disputed deadlines or a problem with the other side is escalated to the attorney with the conversation attached. Every answer is logged with its source passage so the attorney can audit what was said (N.J. RPC 5.3). Documents stay in the firm's own storage with the agent on a zero-retention, tenant-isolated deployment.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: This is not a chatbot over a public FAQ: it needs matter-level state, a document store the firm controls, permissions so client A never sees client B, and retrieval restricted to the firm's own materials with citations the attorney can check. Off-the-shelf assistants have no notion of a closing checklist or of privilege, and the measured hallucination rates in both general and legal-vendor tools make an ungated assistant a malpractice exposure rather than a saving. It also has to write into whatever the firm already uses (Outlook, Word, shared drive, e-sign), which is the integration work.

impact_estimate.range: Roughly $3,000-$15,000/yr of attorney and staff time moved off repetitive status calls and document chasing (2-5 hours/week at $30.33-$77.61/hr), with the larger, unquantified effect being fewer 'nobody told me' complaints - the failure mode behind the firm's two worst public reviews.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Assumes 20-50 active matters a year across closings, probate and business sales (inference - no volume data is public) and 2-4 status contacts per matter, each taking 5-10 minutes. The high end assumes the attorney handles a third of those himself at the NJ lawyer median of $161,430 (=$77.61/hr); the low end assumes a legal secretary at $63,080 (=$30.33/hr) handles all of them. Wage figures: BLS OEWS May 2025 via O*NET, NJ statewide. No reduction in malpractice exposure is quantified.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3-4 weeks on one matter type (residential purchase): a 10-step milestone checklist, six client-facing templates written and approved by the attorney, a document request link with receipt logging, a client Q&A agent restricted to that matter's file plus the firm FAQ, an escalation queue, and an audit log of every answer with its source - measured against the current status-call count for the same period.

lead_score.rationale: Pain (23/30): the front-door failure is directly observed rather than inferred - no form, no tel: link, no viewport meta, an unclaimed 3.0 profile with 4 reviews, and two different addresses for one practice - and the communication problems are corroborated by the firm's own reviews and the owner's first-person promises. It is not higher because there is no volume, fee or revenue data and the review base is four reviews, so the size of the loss is inferred. Fit (17/20): capabilities A, C and G map cleanly onto a solo practice with a tiny legacy stack. The weak fit is E, and no physical/edge avenue applies - this is a third-floor law-office suite with no fleet, kitchen, dock or shop floor, so cameras and sensors would have no operational purpose and would only raise N.J.S.A. 45:5A-2 alarm-business licensing questions for no return (no avenues.json was supplied for this batch either). D is only partially applicable because there is little internal to integrate beyond email, calendar and a shared drive. Ability to pay (9/20): a solo practitioner with dormant marketing, a consumer aol.com address and no published fees; a 30-year real-estate practice can fund a small engagement, but nothing public supports a large one. Ease (13/15): one decision maker, no procurement, no IT department, nothing to migrate - the G work is days, and the A/C pilots touch one calendar and one document store. Strategic (14/15): an unclaimed profile, a non-responsive static site and phone-only intake is the default state of thousands of solo and small NJ firms, so the front-door-plus-intake package becomes a repeatable product. Suggested sequence: fix the front door first (it is cheap and everything else depends on a path customers can actually use), then the intake and scheduling agent, then the status/knowledge agent once real matters flow through a queue. Evidence is strong for the front door but thin for operating volumes, so price the pilot small and confirm matter counts on the first visit.

best_evidence_signal: A 'FREE consultation' phone number baked into a header image, zero forms, zero input fields and zero tel: links on the contact page, and a Google profile still marked 'Claim this business' at 3.0 from 4 reviews - https://www.njrealtylawyer.com/contact-us.php
